title: The moderns: cooperating grace produces free consent
source_text: XLVI. Consequenter autem per gratiam cooperantem intelligunt illam quae in nobis producit liberum illum voluntatis consensum, quo vocationi divinae obsequimur, aliosque deinceps voluntatis nostrae actus, quibus in bono pergimus, magisque ac magis ad Deum convertimur. Illam vero vocari dicunt non operantem, sed cooperantem, quoniam libere cum ea concurrimus; nec actus illi qui ei tribuuntur, a sola gratia procedunt, sed etiam a nostro libero Arbitrio.
pass_a_gloss: XLVI. But consequently by cooperating grace they understand that which produces in us that free consent of the will, by which we obey the divine calling, and the other acts of our will thereafter, by which we go on in good, and are more and more turned to God. But they say it is called not operating, but cooperating, since we freely concur with it; nor do those acts which are attributed to it, proceed from grace alone, but also from our free Choice.
pass_b_english: Thesis XLVI. Accordingly, by cooperating grace they mean the grace that produces in us the free consent of the will by which we obey God's call, and the further acts of our will by which we keep on in good and turn more and more to God.
They say it is called cooperating rather than operating because we concur with it freely, and the acts credited to it come not from grace alone but also from our free choice.
